findings.text: A new test module whose net-new coverage is one case, and whose other two cases duplicate an existing module verbatim. tests/test_compile_abort_probe_exit.py carries a helper `_sample_a_child` and the functions test_failed_child_fails_the_wrapper and test_successful_child_leaves_the_wrapper_at_zero that are byte-for-byte the same bodies (same names, same assertions, same argv including -- /bin/sh -c) as tests/test_compile_abort_probe.py, which c1af3a06d added on 2026-09-21 and which already pins both directions. The only new assertion in the node's whole deliverable is the exit-3 case in test_the_wrapper_carries_an_arbitrary_child_status. The node discloses this in the manifest follow_ons (duplicate-coverage review) and in evidence_inputs, and its fence named the new file, so it had no in-fence way to extend the existing file; the reuse cost is nevertheless real and the coordinator now carries two modules with two identically named tests, which is what the follow-on asks it to consolidate. The plan and evidence landing paragraphs describe the new file as pinning the contract in both directions plus an arbitrary status without saying in that sentence that both directions were already pinned verbatim by the module documented one paragraph above, so a reader skimming only the new paragraph over-counts the module's marginal coverage. test_failed_child_fails_the_wrapper now exists in two modules, so a failure line naming it does not by itself say which file reddened.

justifications.durability: Every artefact the manifest cites is present on disk under the run directory and I read each one directly: gate-green-exit-status.log (header line naming revision, tree and command; tail 3 passed EXIT=0), gate-negative-control.log (declared mutation on its first line; F.F body; 2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1), and the target worktree itself at 7f0207965..e0b686d22. The manifest's numbers reproduce: the artifacts line lists three cases matching the exit codes 7/0/3 in the test file, the tests line names the exact command that the green log's header confirms, and the negative_control_note's two assertion numbers (assert 0 == 7, assert 0 == 3) match the red log line for line. changed_paths is the three files the two commits actually touch, and the probe's absence from it is correct because the mutation was reverted to byte-identity. The record is independently readable, which is what let the prose-vs-log corroboration above be checked at all.
justifications.evidence: The central claim — the wrapper already exits with the sampled child's status, so the defect does not reproduce; and this node adds subprocess coverage — is verified from the artefacts rather than taken on trust. The green gate log's first line names the exact revision (7f0207965bfb513717fac4fa6c33f66047e9d37b), the tree, and the command, and its tail reads 3 passed / EXIT=0. The negative control is a real falsification, not a suite that always passes: its first line repeats the declared string verbatim (restore the unconditional return 0 at the end of the probe main), and its body shows F.F — the exit-7 case at assert 0 == 7, the exit-3 case at assert 0 == 3, and the exit-0 case still passing — which is exactly the two directions the new file claims are distinguished, plus proof the exit-0 case is a genuine two-way assertion rather than a wrapper that always fails. Two claims I re-derived independently both hold: ancestry of c1af3a06d and byte-identity of the probe to HEAD. The one gap is mild: the pre-edit observation that the wrapper around /bin/sh -c exit 7 recorded exit_code 7 and exited 7 is asserted in prose in the plan and manifest with no log of its own; it is corroborated because the green gate's 3-passed result is the same observation on the repaired tree plus the ancestry check that the repair was already in, so the record is not resting on the prose alone. I also re-ran the reviewed gate myself in the reviewed worktree at its tip (revision e0b686d22, command /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_compile_abort_probe_exit.py): 3 passed, EXIT=0, in 5.35s, reproducing the node's green result independently rather than only reading its log.
justifications.fit: The new file, its name (test_compile_abort_probe_exit.py) and its function names describe the behaviour they test, not a plan item; no phase/stage/wave label, no version or plan identifier, and no author attribution appears in the file or in either commit. Both commits use conventional subjects with a real body stating what changed and why (a bodiless commit would have failed review here). The plan and evidence edits add a worker-landing paragraph to the section that already owns this subject rather than opening a new one, and the evidence link uses a project-absolute src to the existing anchor (/nova/evidence/archive/cpu-compile-abort-landed#sampler-exit-status), which resolves to an h2 that exists in the file. Nothing churned the plan-version or plan-modified meta lines.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's measure is met exactly as its SPEC names it: tests/test_compile_abort_probe_exit.py runs the probe as a subprocess around a child exiting 7 and asserts both the receipt field exit_code == 7 and the wrapper process status == 7, runs a child exiting 0 and asserts status 0, passes with its log recorded (3 passed, EXIT=0), and has a declared negative control applied whose red log is on disk. The node also did the half of the CONTRACT-EVIDENCE rule that a re-dispatch of a possibly-stale defect demands: it looked for the recorded defect at base edcba74f0 BEFORE editing, found it already repaired, and said so. I independently confirmed both facts it rests on: `git merge-base --is-ancestor c1af3a06d HEAD` returns true (the one-line return-status repair is landed and reachable), and `git diff HEAD -- benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py` is empty (the probe is byte-identical to its committed state, so nothing was reimplemented). The deduction is for the deliverable's marginal content: the node changed no production behaviour and added one net-new assertion, because the module it added restates an existing module's two cases almost every line.
justifications.scope_discipline: The node stayed strictly inside its fence. Its two commits touch only tests/test_compile_abort_probe_exit.py, docs/plans/cpu-compile-abort.html and docs/evidence/archive/cpu-compile-abort-landed.html — all three under orientation_write_paths — and git status --porcelain on the worktree is empty, so the negative-control mutation on benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py was genuinely reverted and left no dirt. No figure was owed: a wrapper exit status and its two process statuses are a table/log artifact, and the figure rule permits omitting one where a table carries the information. Most importantly the node respected the WHO-CLOSES-THE-NODE contract: its driving followup f-fsa-audit-probe-exit-status is still data-status=open with an empty data-resolved-at, so the node returned the acceptance evidence in evidence_inputs rather than resolving its own followup. The only peripheral note is that its evidence link text (the mapping-count record) names the anchor loosely, but that wording is a pre-existing convention used four times in this file, not something the node introduced.
